title: Entitlement Audit Lifecycle and SDLC Integration Guide
author: Priya Kumar
summary: This guide defines the lifecycle for entitlements (RBAC and delegated access), how entitlement changes must be captured in audit logs, the retention and evidence requirements for compliance reviews, and the SDLC controls required before changes are promoted to production. It outlines runbook steps for evidence collection during incidents and a formal exceptions workflow for short-lived deviations.
background: Redwood operates in mixed deployment environments (hosted, dedicated, private). Access changes and delegated permissions are a high source of compliance risk because they span control planes (console, private control plane, IAM integrations). Operationalizing a repeatable entitlement–audit workflow reduces time-to-evidence and prevents gaps during regulatory reviews.
scope: Applies to all services and control planes managed by Redwood: console web UI, private control plane connectors (SAML/SCIM), service-to-service roles, and operator tooling. Does not replace data subject-specific legal retention decisions documented in data-residency policies, but defines technical evidence retention for entitlement and auth telemetry.
definitions: Entitlement: a grant of permission to perform actions on a resource. Evidence artifact: logged event or exported record that demonstrates the state of an entitlement at a point in time. Authority owner: team responsible for the policy and rules that justify the entitlement (e.g., Platform Security for admin roles).
roles_and_responsibilities:
- Platform Security: approves high-risk role templates and reviews exceptions.
- Identity & Access team: implements SCIM/SAML mappings; owns provisioning pipelines.
- SRE/Infra: ensures forwarding and integrity of audit streams to central logging.
- Product engineering: requests role templates and provides justification for new permissions.
- Compliance: defines evidence retention windows and audit criteria for external audits.
authorization_lifecycle:
1) Request: engineer files an Access Request in the access system with justification and target resources.
2) Approval: authority owner approves or denies; approval recorded as a signed artifact (ticket id + approver).
3) Provisioning: SCIM/SAML or IAM Automation performs change; system emits entitlement-change events.
4) Verification: automated verifier checks effective permissions (simulated subject access) and records result.
5) Monitoring: continuous entitlement drift detection runs daily and logs findings.
6) Deprovisioning: scheduled expiry or manual removal with recorded event.
7) Review: quarterly entitlement reviews for high-risk roles.

Each step MUST be associated with a unique correlation id that is propagated into audit logs and trace headers to enable end-to-end reconstruction.
audit_integration_steps:
- Mandatory audit event types: entitlement.requested, entitlement.approved, entitlement.provisioned, entitlement.verified, entitlement.revoked, entitlement.reviewed.
- Event schema (JSON): timestamp, actor_id, actor_type, action, resource, role_template, correlation_id, evidence_ticket_id, outcome (success|failure), signing_hash.
- Logging sinks: events are forwarded to the structured-audit pipeline (secure S3 bucket + elasticsearch index) and to the streaming SIEM.
- Integrity: events must be signed with a service key; consumers validate signatures before marking evidence as complete.
- Completeness SLO: 99.99% of entitlement lifecycle events must arrive at the evidence store within 5 minutes of the action. Missed events trigger an automated reconciliation job that attempts to replay from the service event journal.
- Retention tagging: every event must include a retention_label that maps to legal/compliance retention policies (e.g., "standard-2y", "gdpr-legal-hold").
evidence_collection_matrix:
Table: Evidence types and minimum retention
- Role template definition (source-of-truth YAML): retention standard-7y (string)
- Approval ticket or signed artifact: retention standard-7y (string)
- Provisioning event (audit log): retention standard-7y (string)
- Verification report (automated check): retention standard-2y (string)
- Quarterly review outcome: retention standard-3y (string)

Note: For customer-specific private deployments, evidence retention may be adjusted by contract. When in doubt, follow the longer retention label and consult Legal.
retention_and_data_residency_guidelines:
- Where logs cross borders: tag events with region and apply the customer's data residency policy.
- Minimal retention windows are expressed as retention_label values. Enforcement is performed by the evidence orchestration service during lifecycle events.
- Legal holds override scheduled deletion: when a matter is opened, the retention engine will set a hold flag and replicate evidence to the compliance vault until release.
- Encryption: audit archives must be encrypted with KMS keys scoped per-region/tenant; key rotation must be recorded in the evidence store.
sdlc_controls_for_auth_changes:
- Branching: all role-template changes must be made in the 'auth' monorepo under a feature branch.
- Review: Pull Request must include: 1) justification, 2) test plan for verifier, 3) list of affected services, 4) risk category tag.
- CI gates: unit tests for schema, static analysis for least-privilege linter, and an integration test that exercises provisioning against a staging IAM simulator.
- Staged rollout: role-template promotions follow canary -> region-wide -> global with rollout policy expressed in the role metadata.
- Deployment blocking: any change marked high-risk requires a Security CLA (design review) and an on-call Security reviewer before merge.
incident_response_alignment:
- When an incident involves entitlement misuse, preserve: 1) all entitlement.* events, 2) auth token issuance logs, 3) session recordings (if present), 4) provisioning system traces.
- Incident Triage steps: 1) capture correlation_id(s) from initial detection, 2) run rapid-replay from event journal for the correlation window, 3) create a Forensic Evidence bundle (manifest + signed logs) and register it with Legal for chain-of-custody.
- Forensic SLA: preservation bundle must be produced within 8 hours for P1 incidents.
- Escalation: if evidence indicates cross-account or cross-region exfiltration, notify Compliance and Legal and escalate to Product Security for containment guidance.
exception_handling_process:
1) Submit Exception Request: include scope, risk mitigation, duration, compensating controls.
2) Risk Owner Review: Platform Security assigns residual risk and mandatory compensating controls.
3) Approval: CISO or delegated approver signs the exception with an expiry date.
4) Implementation: change is annotated in the entitlements catalog and an automated guard rail is created (e.g., alert on activity).
5) Revalidation: exceptions >90 days auto-fail unless reapproved.

All exceptions become part of quarterly compliance evidence exports and must include a post-implementation verification artifact.
implementation_checklist:
- Instrument entitlement events with correlation_id and retention_label.
- Route events to structured-audit pipeline and SIEM.
- Ensure KMS per-region key scoping for audit archives.
- Add CI gates and canary steps for role-template changes.
- Configure legal-hold integration with the evidence orchestration service.
- Document exception artifacts and ensure automated tagging.
- Run an annual game-day simulating an entitlement misuse incident to validate forensic playbooks.
examples_and_snippets:
1) Example audit event JSON:
{
  "timestamp": "2026-01-15T14:23:05Z",
  "actor_id": "u-2345",
  "actor_type": "user",
  "action": "entitlement.provisioned",
  "resource": "project:billing-service",
  "role_template": "billing-admin",
  "correlation_id": "corr-6b9f3e",
  "evidence_ticket_id": "ACC-1123",
  "outcome": "success"
}

2) Example retention label mapping YAML:
retention_labels:
  standard-2y: 2 years
  standard-3y: 3 years
  standard-7y: 7 years
  gdpr-legal-hold: indefinite

3) CLI to request evidence bundle (example):
$ rwd-evidence collect --start 2026-01-15T00:00:00Z --end 2026-01-15T23:59:59Z --correlation corr-6b9f3e --output /tmp/bundle-acc-1123.tar.gz
next_steps:
- Run a cross-team workshop (Platform Security, Identity, SRE, Legal, Product) to validate CI gating and evidence tags.
- Implement correlation id propagation in the auth SDK by Q2 2026.
- Pilot the retention_label enforcement in the evidence orchestration service on a non-production tenant.
